def: The part of the system that manages the account lifecycle after the loan is disbursed: tracking balances, calculating interest, processing payments, producing statements. In VLP this is the LAS module.

When a product attracts a higher than normal share of risky customers. It happens when price does not distinguish risk: high-risk customers come because the price is cheap relative to their risk, and low-risk customers leave because it is expensive relative to theirs.

alt: Vietnamese: đánh giá khả năng chi trả
def: The process of determining whether a customer can really repay the loan without undue difficulty, as distinct from checking eligibility. It covers income verification, listing existing obligations, a residual income check and a stress test.

Data that does not come from a traditional credit bureau: mobile operator data, e-wallet transactions, bill payment history, in-app behaviour. Used to score thin-file customers, and only with explicit consent.

alt: Vietnamese: trả dần (khấu hao khoản vay)
def: Paying down principal over time. With an equal-instalment loan, each instalment contains a portion of principal and a portion of interest; the interest share is largest at the start and the principal share grows over time.

alt: Supplement · Vietnamese: sản phẩm bổ sung
def: The module managing add-on products attached to a loan contract (insurance, warranties, payment protection). Lifecycle: INITIAL → REGISTERED → ACTIVE → TERMINATED; activated when LAS emits the FIRST_PRINCIPAL_TX_CHARGED event.

alt: Annual Percentage Rate · Vietnamese: lãi suất phần trăm năm
def: The annual cost of credit, including every mandatory fee rather than just the nominal rate. In this book, APR = the monthly IRR × 12 (no compounding); the compounded measure is the EIR. Lan's loan has a nominal rate of 18% but an APR of 20.10% because of the 200,000 VND appraisal fee.

A mechanism that automatically debits the customer's account on the due date. When direct debit is on by default (customers can turn it off), usage at Vela Finance is 82%, against 45% when customers have to sign up themselves.

alt: BaaS · Vietnamese: ngân hàng như một dịch vụ
def: A model providing financial infrastructure (licence, core banking, compliance) to third parties via API, so fintechs can build financial products without holding a banking licence themselves.
A credit score calculated from behavioural data (app usage, payment habits, mobile operator data) rather than bureau data alone. Especially useful for thin-file customers.

alt: Quasi-hyperbolic discounting · Vietnamese: mô hình β-δ
def: Laibson's (1997) model of present bias: every future benefit is discounted by an extra factor β < 1, while the present is not; δ is the ordinary time discount factor.
The monthly loop: interest and fees accrue, EOM creates the instalment and the statement, the payment falls due, the payment is received and matched, and DPD is tracked if it is unpaid.

alt: Buy Now Pay Later · Vietnamese: mua trước trả sau
def: A form of credit that lets people buy now and pay in instalments later, usually 3-6 instalments, often at a nominal 0% interest. Revenue comes from merchant fees and, in many markets, from a "processing fee" charged to the buyer.

alt: Vietnamese: trung tâm thông tin tín dụng
def: An organization that collects and provides credit histories. In Vietnam this is the CIC (National Credit Information Centre); internationally there are Experian, TransUnion and Equifax.

alt: Customer Acquisition Cost · Vietnamese: chi phí thu hút khách hàng
def: The total cost of gaining a new customer: marketing, sales, file processing. CAC determines the minimum loan amount for a loan to be profitable.

Checking whether predicted probabilities match actual rates. For example, customers with 420 points are predicted to have a PD of 2.4%; if their actual default rate is around 2.4%, the model is well calibrated.

alt: Customer Lifetime Value · Vietnamese: giá trị vòng đời khách hàng
def: The present value of the net profit a customer brings over the whole relationship: the sum over years of that year's profit times the probability the customer is still there, discounted to the present.
The mental effort needed to process information and make a decision. High cognitive load pushes people towards System 1 thinking and lowers the quality of financial decisions.
The process of contacting, negotiating with and recovering debt from overdue customers, from early reminders, payment arrangements and hardship support to litigation or debt sale.
A mechanism that lets people voluntarily limit their future choices to keep to their present intentions. Examples: a savings lock, a pledge to use a bonus to pay down debt.
The risk of a portfolio depending too heavily on one sector, one employer or one region. When that point of concentration takes a shock, the whole portfolio is hit at once.
The entity linking an account to a tariff code and version, which determines the interest rate and fees applying to that account.

What the lender pays to raise the money it lends: bank borrowing costs, bond yields. The equity portion is accounted for through the target ROE. The book's examples use 8.5%/year for the debt portion.
A single number summarizing a customer's credit risk, calculated from payment history, balances, length of credit history, credit mix and recent inquiries.

alt: Vietnamese: tỷ lệ sử dụng hạn mức
def: The balance divided by the credit limit. A high ratio is a sign of financial stress; it is one of the components of the FICO score.
The LAS entity tracking an account's current balance by type: principal, interest, fees, penalties.

alt: 30/360 day count · Vietnamese: quy ước ngày 30/360
def: The interest convention used in VLP's examples: every month counts as 30 days and the year as 360, so one full month's interest = balance × annual rate / 12. Unlike Actual/365, which uses actual days. Configured through AnnualRateDayCount.D30_360 in the tariff.

alt: Vietnamese: mẫu thiết kế lừa dối
def: An interface design that deliberately leads users towards decisions not in their interest: fake countdown timers, hidden fees, hard-to-find decline buttons.
A change over time in the distribution of input data. A PSI above 0.25 is a major change, and the model may no longer be valid.
A customer having several BNPL plans or loans with several providers, each of which sees only part of the picture. The real DTI is higher than any single provider knows.
Usually defined as DPD 90+ at any point in an observation window (e.g. 24 months). It can be stricter (write-off) or looser (DPD 30+) depending on the purpose.
The state of a loan that is past due but not yet in default, usually DPD 1-89.
A policy that is neutral in form but affects a protected group disproportionately, even without any intent to discriminate.

alt: Days Past Due · Vietnamese: số ngày quá hạn
def: The number of days since the due date of the earliest unpaid overdue instalment. DPD 0 means current. A key metric for collections, loan classification and IFRS 9.

The module that aggregates data from many internal systems into XML for document generation (contracts, annexes). It is not a disbursement module. Plugin architecture with providers such as AgreementDataSourceProvider and ContractDataSourceProvider.

alt: Debt-to-Income · Vietnamese: tỷ lệ nợ trên thu nhập
def: Total monthly debt obligations divided by monthly income. Lan's loan has a DTI of 7.7% (1,696,080 / 22,000,000).

alt: Vietnamese: lý thuyết hai hệ tư duy
def: Kahneman's framework: System 1 is fast, automatic and intuitive; System 2 is slow, deliberate and logical. Financial decisions are often driven by System 1.

alt: Exposure at Default · Vietnamese: dư nợ tại thời điểm vỡ nợ
def: The amount still owed when the customer defaults. For an instalment loan, EAD is usually the remaining principal balance at that point, which is less than the original loan amount.

alt: Vietnamese: hệ thống cảnh báo sớm
def: A system that detects customers at risk of not repaying before DPD appears, so intervention can start early, in tiers from a gentle reminder to hardship support.

alt: EIR · Vietnamese: lãi suất thực tế
def: The compounded annual rate corresponding to the periodic IRR: EIR = (1 + monthly IRR)^12 − 1. Always higher than the APR (= monthly IRR × 12) when the IRR is positive.

alt: Expected Loss · Vietnamese: tổn thất dự kiến
def: EL = PD × LGD × EAD. The average expected loss, built into the product price: it is a priced-in cost, not a risk.
Integrating financial products into non-financial platforms, so customers use credit in context (at checkout, when booking a service) without switching to a financial app.

alt: Equated Monthly Instalment · Vietnamese: khoản trả góp đều hằng tháng
def: The fixed amount paid each month, consisting of a portion of principal and a portion of interest, calculated with the PMT formula. Lan's loan has an EMI of 1,696,080 VND.

alt: End of Month · Vietnamese: xử lý cuối tháng
def: The end-of-period batch job: calculating interest, creating instalments, charging fees, generating statement data, updating balances. In VLP it runs in parallel by partition.

alt: Vietnamese: drift của biến đầu vào
def: A form of data drift: the distribution of an input feature changes over time, measured by the PSI of each feature.

alt: Vietnamese: xây dựng biến đầu vào
def: Turning raw data into features suitable for a model: WOE transformations, ratios, time windows.
Infrastructure for computing, storing and serving input features to models: centralized, versioned, point-in-time correct, consistent between training and serving.

The most widely used credit score in the US, from the Fair Isaac Corporation, on a 300-850 scale. Five groups of factors: payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of history 15%, credit mix 10%, new credit 10%.
Deliberately giving false information to obtain credit. Forms include application fraud, identity theft, synthetic identities, velocity fraud and AI-generated documents.

A measure of a credit model's discriminatory power: Gini = 2 × AUROC − 1, on a 0-1 scale. Above 0.45 is usually considered acceptable, above 0.60 good. Gini measures ranking ability, not the percentage of defaults explained.
A period after the due date during which payment is still accepted without a late fee. Its length is a product configuration parameter.

When an LLM produces content that is wrong but sounds convincing. Especially dangerous in finance (wrong figures, wrong policies). Mitigated with RAG and the rule that every number must come from the database.

alt: Vietnamese: chương trình hỗ trợ khó khăn
def: Solutions for customers in financial difficulty: payment holidays, term extensions, temporary rate reductions. The aim is to help the customer cure and keep the relationship, rather than collecting at any cost.
The tendency to overweight short-term benefits and costs relative to long-term ones. It explains why people "always plan to start saving next month". See the β-δ Model.
Performing an operation once or many times gives the same result. Mandatory for payment APIs and batch jobs to avoid duplicate charges or disbursements.

alt: International Financial Reporting Standard 9 · Vietnamese: chuẩn mực báo cáo tài chính quốc tế số 9
def: The accounting standard for financial instruments, requiring provisions based on expected credit loss (ECL) in three stages: Stage 1 (performing, 12-month ECL), Stage 2 (significant increase in credit risk, lifetime ECL), Stage 3 (credit-impaired, lifetime ECL).

alt: Vietnamese: bộ nhớ đệm phân tán Infinispan
def: A distributed in-memory cache. In VLP, LOS uses embedded Infinispan to hold workflow state between asynchronous steps, with 7 named caches: zeebeChooseOfferCache, chooseOfferCache, loanPurposeCache, generateAgreementCache, signAgreementCache, rejectSupplementCache, cancelSupplementCache.

alt: IV · Vietnamese: giá trị thông tin
def: A measure of a variable's predictive power in credit scoring. IV < 0.02: no value; 0.02-0.10: weak; 0.10-0.30: medium; > 0.30: strong; > 0.50: suspiciously strong, check for data leakage.

alt: Vietnamese: tổng hợp kỳ trả góp
def: A denormalized aggregate entity in LAS summarizing an account's instalment plan. It may only be refreshed after every child instalment has been saved (see bug VLP-670 in Chapter 16).

alt: Internal Rate of Return · Vietnamese: tỷ suất hoàn vốn nội bộ
def: The discount rate at which the net present value of all cash flows is zero. Used to calculate the APR and EIR from the cash the customer actually receives and pays.

alt: Vietnamese: cho vay theo phán đoán
def: Traditional lending based on a loan officer's judgement: inconsistent, unscalable, with hidden bias and no audit trail. Gradually replaced by statistical scoring.
The largest gap between the cumulative distributions of good and bad customers by score: KS = max(cumulative %Bad − cumulative %Good). KS > 30% is good.

alt: Loss Given Default · Vietnamese: tỷ lệ tổn thất khi vỡ nợ
def: The share of EAD the lender actually loses after recoveries: LGD = 1 − recovery rate. Typically 55-70% for unsecured consumer loans; the book's examples use 62%.

alt: Large Language Model · Vietnamese: mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn
def: An AI model trained on very large amounts of text that understands and generates text. In lending: document processing, customer service, knowledge management, always with guardrails against hallucination.

The stateless loan origination orchestrator: it receives the application, calls the modules for checks, scoring and pricing, then creates the contract and account. Uses async controllers and Infinispan, not a BPMN engine, for the main flow.

Losses hurt more than equal gains please. As estimated by Tversky and Kahneman (1992), λ ≈ 2.25: losing 100,000 feels as bad as gaining about 225,000 feels good. Used when designing payment reminder messages, provided the numbers are true.
The tendency to treat money differently according to its mental "account" (salary, bonus, savings). Bonus money is usually spent faster than the same amount of salary (Thaler).

The risk of using a wrong model, or using a right model wrongly: model errors, implementation errors, misuse. Governed by a three-layer MRM framework: development validation, independent validation, ongoing monitoring.
When shielded from the consequences, people tend to take more risk. In lending: a borrower who has received the money may misuse it; a guaranteed lender may lend too recklessly.
The difference between interest income from lending and the interest cost of funding, divided by average interest-earning assets. A basic measure of a lender's profitability.
In Vietnam, debt in groups 3 to 5 under Circular 31/2024/TT-NHNN, essentially more than 90 days overdue. NPL ratio = NPLs / total loans.
A small, non-coercive design intervention that steers behaviour in the desired direction. The default option is the most powerful nudge (Thaler and Sunstein, 2008).

A framework letting customers share their financial data with third parties via API with consent, enabling better credit assessment and boosting competition. In Vietnam there is Circular 64/2024/TT-NHNN on Open API.
The tendency to overestimate the chance of good things and underestimate the chance of bad things happening to oneself. Borrowers underestimate the risk of having difficulty repaying.

Letting the customer pause payments for a number of periods (usually 1-3 months), with due dates moved later. Whether interest keeps accruing or is waived depends on configuration (the payholInterestWaiving flag in VLP).

alt: Probability of Default · Vietnamese: xác suất vỡ nợ
def: The probability that a customer defaults within a given period. PD × LGD × EAD = EL.

alt: Periodic payment · Vietnamese: khoản trả mỗi kỳ
def: The amount paid each period on an equal-instalment loan: PMT = P × r(1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n − 1), where r is the periodic rate. Lan's loan: PMT = 1,696,080 VND, with the final instalment adjusted for rounding to 1,696,077.
The tendency to overweight immediate benefits and costs relative to the future, leading to too much borrowing and too little saving. See the β-δ Model.
An ML model estimating how likely a customer is to respond (accept an offer, buy a product). It should be combined with risk so as not to target people who are in a hurry.
Kahneman and Tversky (1979): people judge outcomes as changes relative to a reference point, not by absolute value, and losses weigh more than equivalent gains.

alt: Population Stability Index · Vietnamese: chỉ số ổn định tập khách hàng
def: A measure of distribution change between training data and current data. PSI < 0.10: stable; 0.10-0.25: moderate change, monitor closely; > 0.25: major change, review the model.

The module that stores and manages the lifecycle of quotes produced by QCE. Its main entity is the SalesQuote with arrangements for amount, interest and fees. LOS calls QST to retrieve quotes; QST publishes CloudEvents via Kafka when a quote changes.

An architecture combining an LLM with information retrieval: before answering, the system retrieves relevant documents and the LLM answers only from their content. Reduces hallucination, and makes answers consistent and sourced.

alt: Vietnamese: định giá dựa trên rủi ro
def: Higher-risk customers pay higher rates, so that the price reflects expected loss. In VLP: Prime 15%, Standard 18%, Sub-prime 21%.

alt: Return on Equity · Vietnamese: tỷ suất lợi nhuận trên vốn chủ sở hữu
def: Profit divided by equity. The target ROE determines the profit component that must be in the interest rate (Chapter 12 uses 18% on 15% equity).
The traditional scoring model: logistic regression on WOE-transformed variables, scaled to points with an anchor and a PDO. Easy to explain and favoured by regulators.
A method of explaining a model's prediction by splitting it into additive contributions from each variable. The basis for generating specific rejection reasons.

A stateless routing module: it receives loan processing requests from LOS and forwards them to the backends (LAS, CTM, AOS, CTS, PDC, ADR, QST, LBS...) through 9 FeignClient connectors, with Resilience4j circuit breakers. It has no database of its own.

alt: Vietnamese: kiểm tra sức chịu đựng
def: Assessing a portfolio or model under adverse scenarios: recession, a spike in unemployment, rising rates. The results determine the capital plan.
The customer segment scoring below the Standard cut-off. In VLP: 340-379 points, 21%/year interest, lower maximum limits.
The risk of rare, extreme events. Ordinary risk management optimizes for the average; tail risk management focuses on surviving the worst case.

alt: Vietnamese: thiết kế dựa trên biểu phí
def: An architecture in which business rules (rates, fees, limits) live in versioned configuration with effective dates rather than being hard-coded, so they can change without a deployment.

alt: Vietnamese: hồ sơ tín dụng mỏng
def: Customers with little or no credit history, who cannot be scored with traditional bureau data. They need alternative data or behavioural scores.

alt: Vietnamese: giá trị thời gian của tiền
def: A dong today is worth more than a dong in the future because it can be invested to earn a return. The foundation of NPV, IRR and the annuity formula.

alt: Unexpected Loss · Vietnamese: tổn thất ngoài dự kiến
def: The amount by which actual losses can exceed EL. EL is covered by price; UL is covered by capital.

alt: Vietnamese: ngày canh gác "không bao giờ tới"
def: A far-future date used for records with no end date, so date range queries stay simple (WHERE validTo >= :today) instead of checking for NULL. In VLP: AccountParameter.validTo and AccountService.endDate use 3000-01-01 (DateUtil.UNREACHABLE_FUTURE_DATE, with NULL in the DB converted by NullDateToFarFutureConverter); PostingUnit.firstPrescribeDate uses 3333-01-01 for "not yet prescribed". Two different values for two different purposes, and confusing them is a classic source of query bugs.
Submitting many loan applications to many providers in a short time, before they can see each other's approvals. Detected through recent inquiry counts, shared blacklists and device fingerprinting.

Tracking the performance of groups of loans by disbursement month, for example comparing the DPD 30+ rate after 6 months of the January cohort with February and March. Detects model drift and portfolio quality trends.

alt: Weight of Evidence · Vietnamese: trọng số bằng chứng
def: A transformation for scoring variables: WOE_i = ln(%Bad_i / %Good_i). Negative means the bin leans towards good customers, positive towards bad ones.

The accounting decision to take a loan no longer expected to be recovered off the balance sheet, using the provisions already made. The threshold is a configuration parameter (e.g. DPD 90 for unsecured consumer loans). Write-off is not debt forgiveness: the obligation to repay remains and collection continues.
A popular gradient boosting library for tabular data, usually giving high accuracy in credit scoring, handling missing values and training fast.

A BPMN workflow engine (Camunda). In VLP it is used only for scoring in the chooseOffer step (the zeebe-integration profile), not as the main origination orchestrator. POSITIVE/NEGATIVE results are sent back to LOS via RabbitMQ.
